   1"""Tests for the ItsTime class which handles ITS (International Timing System) time
   2operations.
   3
   4This module contains a comprehensive test suite for the ItsTime class from the step_cloud_schemas
   5package. The tests verify the functionality of time conversions between different time formats:
   6
   7    - Unix epoch time (seconds since January 1, 1970, UTC)
   8    - ITS time (TAI milliseconds since January 1, 2004, ETSI ``TimestampIts``)
   9    - ISO 8601 formatted time strings (UTC)
  10
  11The test suite covers:
  12
  13    #. Class initialization and proper attribute setting
  14    #. Comparison operations (equality, less than)
  15    #. Arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction)
  16    #. Time conversion methods (between epoch, ITS, and ISO formats)
  17    #. String representation and formatting
  18    #. Delta time calculations
  19    #. Error handling and edge cases
  20    #. TAI conformance (normative vectors, leap-second boundaries)
  21    #. The ``LeapSeconds`` singleton (configuration, expiry, background refresh,
  22       thread and coroutine safety)
  23
  24The tests use fixtures with predefined timestamps to ensure consistent and reproducible
  25testing outcomes across all test functions. ``test/conftest.py`` pins the clock and
  26blocks the network for every test.
  27"""
  28# ruff: noqa: ARG002, N801, PLR2004, S101, SLF001
  29# N801: ``Test_OffsetTable`` mirrors the private ``_OffsetTable`` class name.
  30# ARG002: fixtures such as ``expired`` and ``clock`` are requested for their side effects.
  31
  32# Standard Library Imports
  33import asyncio
  34import dataclasses
  35import datetime
  36import logging
  37import pathlib
  38import threading
  39from collections.abc import Callable
  40from unittest.mock import MagicMock
  41
  42# Third Party Imports
  43import pytest
  44from leapseconddata import LeapSecondData
  45from pytest_mock import MockerFixture
  46
  47# step_cloud_schemas Package Imports
  48from step_cloud_schemas import ItsTime, LeapSeconds, SingletonMeta
  49from step_cloud_schemas.classes.its_time import (
  50    _MAX_UTC_ITS_MS,
  51    _MIN_UTC_ITS_MS,
  52    _is_expired,
  53    _is_newer,
  54    _OffsetTable,
  55    _read_bundled_leap_seconds,
  56)
  57
  58ITS_EPOCH_UNIX_MS = 1072915200000
  59"""2004-01-01T00:00:00Z in Unix milliseconds."""
  60
  61LEAP_SECONDS_SINCE_ITS_EPOCH_MS = 5000
  62"""TAI is ahead of UTC, since the ITS epoch, by the 5 leap seconds inserted on
  632006-01-01, 2009-01-01, 2012-07-01, 2015-07-01 and 2017-01-01 (IERS Bulletin C)."""
  64
  65TEST_LEAP_SECONDS_FILE = (
  66    pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "leap-seconds-test.list"
  67)
  68"""Frozen copy of leap-seconds.list, valid until 2027-06-28."""
  69
  70_ORIGINAL_UTC_NOW = LeapSeconds.__dict__["_utc_now"]
  71"""Unpatched ``LeapSeconds._utc_now``, captured before ``conftest`` pins it."""
  72
  73
  74def _utc_its_ms(iso: str) -> int:
  75    """Return the UTC milliseconds elapsed between the ITS epoch and ``iso``.
  76
  77    Computed with plain ``datetime`` arithmetic, independently of the code under test.
  78
  79    Args:
  80        iso (str): An ISO 8601 UTC string ending with ``Z``.
  81
  82    Returns:
  83        int: Milliseconds since 2004-01-01T00:00:00Z on the UTC scale.
  84    """
  85    moment = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(iso)
  86    epoch = datetime.datetime(2004, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
  87    return (moment - epoch) // datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1)
  88
  89
  90def _iso_ms(moment: datetime.datetime) -> str:
  91    """Format ``moment`` as ``YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ``.
  92
  93    Args:
  94        moment (datetime.datetime): A timezone-aware UTC datetime.
  95
  96    Returns:
  97        str: The ISO 8601 string with millisecond precision.
  98    """
  99    return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"
 100

 103    ("2006-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", 1),

 105    ("2012-07-01T00:00:00.000Z", 3),
 106    ("2015-07-01T00:00:00.000Z", 4),
 107    ("2017-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", 5),
 108]
 109"""First UTC instant after each leap second inserted since the ITS epoch, paired with
 110the number of leap seconds inserted up to and including it."""
 111

 294        ids=["its_epoch", "normative_2007", "2026", "2026_round_down", "2026_round_up"],
 295    )
 296    def test__utc_epoch_to_its_ms(
 297        self, iso: str, fraction_s: float, expected_its_ms: int | None
 298    ) -> None:
 299        """Test that ``_utc_epoch_to_its_ms`` rounds the Unix seconds to the
 300        millisecond, shifts them to the ITS epoch and adds the leap-second offset.
 301
 302        Args:
 303            iso (str): The UTC instant, as an ISO 8601 string.
 304            fraction_s (float): Sub-millisecond seconds added to the instant.
 305            expected_its_ms (int | None): The expected TAI ITS milliseconds, or None
 306                to derive it as the UTC value plus the five leap seconds.
 307
 308        Returns:
 309            None
 310        """
 311        epoch = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(iso).timestamp() + fraction_s
 312        if expected_its_ms is None:
 313            expected_its_ms = (
 314                _utc_its_ms(iso)
 315                + round(fraction_s * 1000)
 316                + LEAP_SECONDS_SINCE_ITS_EPOCH_MS
 317            )
 318
 319        assert ItsTime._utc_epoch_to_its_ms(epoch) == expected_its_ms

 478    def test___add__(self, time_its_1_ms: int, delta_time_ms: int) -> None:
 479        """Test the addition operation of ItsTime.
 480
 481        This test case verifies that adding a time delta (in milliseconds) to an
 482        ItsTime object produces a new ItsTime instance with the expected time value.
 483
 484        Asserts:

 486            - The result's internal time value equals the sum of the initial time and delta
 487            - The result is a new object (not the same instance as the original)

 489        Args:

 495        """
 496        its_time = ItsTime(its_time_ms=time_its_1_ms)
 497        result = its_time + delta_time_ms
 498        assert isinstance(result, ItsTime)
 499        assert result._its_time_ms == time_its_1_ms + delta_time_ms
 500        assert result is not its_time

 983            delta_time_ms=delta_ms, epoch=time_epoch_1, module=0x10000
 984        )
 985        assert (
 986            its_time._its_time_ms
 987            == (time_its_1_ms & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0000) + 0x10000 + delta_ms
 988        )

1266    def test_create_from_iso_time_leap_second_boundary_jump(
1267        self, iso_at: str, leap_count: int
1268    ) -> None:
1269        """Test that across each leap second the TAI values differ by 1001 ms for two
1270        UTC instants 1 ms apart, and that both carry the expected offset.
1271
1272        Args:
1273            iso_at (str): The first UTC instant after the inserted leap second.
1274            leap_count (int): The leap seconds inserted up to and including it.

1276        Returns:
1277            None

1281        before = ItsTime.create_from_epoch_ms(epoch_ms=at.epoch_ms - 1)
1282
1283        assert at.its_ms - before.its_ms == 1001
1284        assert at.its_ms == utc_at + leap_count * 1000
1285        assert before.its_ms == utc_at - 1 + (leap_count - 1) * 1000

1426    """Tests for the ``LeapSeconds`` singleton.
1427
1428    Every test runs on a frozen copy of the leap-second file (``test/data``) standing
1429    in for the bundled one, so results do not change when the bundled file is updated.
1430    ``test/conftest.py`` pins the clock and forbids downloads; tests that need an
1431    expired table or a refresh override those defaults.
1432    """

1435    NEWER_VALID_UNTIL = datetime.datetime(2029, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
1436    URLS = ("https://example.invalid/leap-seconds.list",)

1501    @staticmethod
1502    def _join_refresh(leap_seconds: LeapSeconds) -> None:
1503        """Wait for the background refresh thread, if any, to finish.
1504
1505        Args:
1506            leap_seconds (LeapSeconds): The instance owning the thread.
1507
1508        Returns:
1509            None
1510        """
1511        thread = leap_seconds._refresh_thread
1512        if thread is not None:
1513            thread.join(timeout=5)
1514            assert not thread.is_alive()
1515
1516    @staticmethod
1517    def _assert_idle(leap_seconds: LeapSeconds) -> None:
1518        """Assert the lock is free and no refresh is marked as running.
1519
1520        Args:
1521            leap_seconds (LeapSeconds): The instance to check.
1522
1523        Returns:
1524            None
1525        """
1526        assert leap_seconds._lock.acquire(blocking=False)
1527        leap_seconds._lock.release()
1528        assert leap_seconds._refresh_started_at is None
1529
1530    @staticmethod
1531    def _assert_lock_free(leap_seconds: LeapSeconds) -> None:
1532        """Assert the lock can be acquired right away.
1533
1534        Args:
1535            leap_seconds (LeapSeconds): The instance to check.
1536
1537        Returns:
1538            None
1539        """
1540        assert leap_seconds._lock.acquire(blocking=False)
1541        leap_seconds._lock.release()

1927    ) -> None:

1929        mapped to the last millisecond of the preceding second (23:59:59.999).
1930
1931        Args:
1932            iso_at (str): The first UTC instant after the inserted leap second.
1933            leap_count (int): The leap seconds inserted up to and including it.
1934            into_leap_ms (int): Milliseconds elapsed inside the leap second.
1935
1936        Returns:
1937            None
1938        """
1939        utc_at = _utc_its_ms(iso_at)
1940        first_tai_of_leap_second = utc_at + (leap_count - 1) * 1000
1941
1942        result = LeapSeconds().tai_to_utc_ms(first_tai_of_leap_second + into_leap_ms)
1943
1944        assert result == utc_at - 1

2083    ) -> None:

2087        failing background refresh may hold it during the first conversions, so
2088        the conversions are repeated after the refresh is joined (the lock is then

2101
2102        with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger="step_cloud_schemas"):
2103            for _ in range(5):
2104                leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(0)
2105            self._join_refresh(leap_seconds)

2113    def test__warn_expired_once_skipped_when_another_thread_won_the_race(
2114        self, expired: None, data: LeapSecondData, caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture
2115    ) -> None:
2116        """Test that the warning is not duplicated when another thread records it
2117        between the first check and the lock acquisition.
2118
2119        Args:
2120            expired (None): Fixture moving the clock past the expiry.
2121            data (LeapSecondData): The frozen test data.
2122            caplog (pytest.LogCaptureFixture): Fixture capturing log records.
2123
2124        Returns:
2125            None
2126        """
2127        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds(allow_download=False)
2128
2129        class RacingLock:
2130            """A lock whose acquisition simulates another thread warning first."""
2131
2132            def acquire(self, blocking: bool = True) -> bool:
2133                """Record the warning as if made by another thread.
2134
2135                Args:
2136                    blocking (bool): Ignored.
2137
2138                Returns:
2139                    bool: Always True.
2140                """
2141                leap_seconds._expiry_warned_for = data.valid_until
2142                return True
2143
2144            def release(self) -> None:
2145                """Do nothing.
2146
2147                Returns:
2148                    None
2149                """
2150
2151        leap_seconds._lock = RacingLock()  # type: ignore[assignment]
2152
2153        with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger="step_cloud_schemas"):
2154            leap_seconds._warn_expired_once(data)
2155
2156        assert caplog.records == []

2398    def test__maybe_start_refresh_hung_download_replaced_after_stale_timeout(
2399        self,
2400        expired: None,
2401        clock: MagicMock,
2402        mocker: MockerFixture,
2403        data: LeapSecondData,
2404    ) -> None:
2405        """Test that a download still running after ``LEAP_SECONDS_REFRESH_STALE_S``
2406        is considered dead and replaced, that the lock stays free meanwhile, and
2407        that the old worker finishing later does not clear the state of the new one.
2408
2409        Args:
2410            expired (None): Fixture moving the clock past the expiry.
2411            clock (MagicMock): The mocked ``time.monotonic``.
2412            mocker (MockerFixture): pytest-mock fixture.
2413            data (LeapSecondData): The frozen test data.
2414
2415        Returns:
2416            None
2417        """
2418        gates = [threading.Event(), threading.Event()]
2419        entered = [threading.Event(), threading.Event()]
2420        results = [
2421            dataclasses.replace(
2422                data, valid_until=datetime.datetime(2029, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
2423            ),
2424            dataclasses.replace(
2425                data, valid_until=datetime.datetime(2030, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
2426            ),
2427        ]
2428        calls: list[int] = []
2429
2430        def slow_download(*_: object, **__: object) -> LeapSecondData:
2431            """Block until this call's gate opens, then return its result.
2432
2433            Args:
2434                *_ (object): Ignored positional arguments (the source URL).
2435                **__ (object): Ignored keyword arguments.
2436
2437            Returns:
2438                LeapSecondData: The result prepared for this call.
2439            """
2440            index = len(calls)
2441            calls.append(index)
2442            entered[index].set()
2443            assert gates[index].wait(timeout=5)
2444            return results[index]
2445
2446        mocker.patch.object(LeapSecondData, "from_url", side_effect=slow_download)
2447        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds(allow_download=True)
2448
2449        leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(0)
2450        assert entered[0].wait(timeout=5)
2451        first_thread = leap_seconds._refresh_thread
2452        assert first_thread is not None
2453        self._assert_lock_free(leap_seconds)
2454
2455        clock.return_value = 1000.0 + LeapSeconds.LEAP_SECONDS_REFRESH_STALE_S - 1
2456        leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(0)
2457        assert len(calls) == 1
2458
2459        clock.return_value = 1000.0 + LeapSeconds.LEAP_SECONDS_REFRESH_STALE_S + 1
2460        leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(0)
2461        assert entered[1].wait(timeout=5)
2462        assert len(calls) == 2
2463
2464        gates[0].set()
2465        first_thread.join(timeout=5)
2466        assert leap_seconds._data is results[0]
2467        assert leap_seconds._refresh_started_at is not None
2468
2469        gates[1].set()
2470        self._join_refresh(leap_seconds)
2471        assert leap_seconds._data is results[1]
2472        self._assert_idle(leap_seconds)

2511    def test__maybe_start_refresh_concurrent_threads_share_one_download(
2512        self,
2513        blocked_download: tuple[threading.Event, Callable[[], int]],
2514        newer_data: LeapSecondData,
2515    ) -> None:
2516        """Test that many threads converting at once on expired data trigger a single
2517        download and all finish while it is still running.
2518
2519        Args:
2520            blocked_download (tuple[threading.Event, Callable[[], int]]): The gate and
2521                the download counter.
2522            newer_data (LeapSecondData): The data the download returns.
2523
2524        Returns:
2525            None
2526        """
2527        gate, download_count = blocked_download
2528        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds(allow_download=True)
2529        thread_count = 16
2530        barrier = threading.Barrier(thread_count)
2531        utc_ms = _utc_its_ms("2026-09-25T12:00:00.000Z")
2532        results: list[int] = []
2533        results_lock = threading.Lock()
2534
2535        def worker() -> None:
2536            """Convert once, after all threads are ready, and store the result.
2537
2538            Returns:
2539                None
2540            """
2541            barrier.wait(timeout=5)
2542            tai_ms = leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms)
2543            with results_lock:
2544                results.append(tai_ms)
2545
2546        threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(thread_count)]
2547        for thread in threads:
2548            thread.start()
2549        for thread in threads:
2550            thread.join(timeout=5)
2551
2552        assert not gate.is_set()
2553        assert not any(thread.is_alive() for thread in threads)
2554        assert results == [utc_ms + 5000] * thread_count
2555
2556        gate.set()
2557        self._join_refresh(leap_seconds)
2558        assert download_count() == 1
2559        assert leap_seconds._data is newer_data

2561    async def test_coroutines_are_not_blocked_by_download(
2562        self, blocked_download: tuple[threading.Event, Callable[[], int]]
2563    ) -> None:
2564        """Test that coroutines converting on expired data keep running (a sibling
2565        coroutine keeps ticking) while the download is blocked.
2566
2567        Args:
2568            blocked_download (tuple[threading.Event, Callable[[], int]]): The gate and
2569                the download counter.
2570
2571        Returns:
2572            None
2573        """
2574        gate, download_count = blocked_download
2575        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds(allow_download=True)
2576        utc_ms = _utc_its_ms("2026-09-25T12:00:00.000Z")
2577        ticks = 0
2578        stop = False
2579
2580        async def ticker() -> None:
2581            """Count event-loop iterations until asked to stop.
2582
2583            Returns:
2584                None
2585            """
2586            nonlocal ticks
2587            while not stop:
2588                ticks += 1
2589                await asyncio.sleep(0)
2590
2591        async def converter() -> list[int]:
2592            """Convert repeatedly, yielding to the event loop between conversions.
2593
2594            Returns:
2595                list[int]: The converted values.
2596            """
2597            converted = []
2598            for _ in range(200):
2599                converted.append(leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms))
2600                await asyncio.sleep(0)
2601            return converted
2602
2603        ticker_task = asyncio.create_task(ticker())
2604        converted = await asyncio.wait_for(converter(), timeout=5)
2605        stop = True
2606        await ticker_task
2607
2608        assert converted == [utc_ms + 5000] * 200
2609        assert ticks >= 100
2610        assert not gate.is_set()
2611        gate.set()
2612        self._join_refresh(leap_seconds)
2613        assert download_count() == 1

2616        self,

2618        newer_data: LeapSecondData,
2619    ) -> None:
2620        """Test coroutines of the running loop, ``asyncio.to_thread`` workers and a
2621        second event loop in another thread converting together: one download, nobody
2622        blocked, and all see the new data once the download completes.
2623
2624        Args:
2625            blocked_download (tuple[threading.Event, Callable[[], int]]): The gate and
2626                the download counter.

2630            None

2632        gate, download_count = blocked_download
2633        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds(allow_download=True)
2634        utc_ms = _utc_its_ms("2026-09-25T12:00:00.000Z")
2635        other_loop_results: list[int] = []
2636
2637        async def other_loop_main() -> None:
2638            """Convert repeatedly on a second event loop running in another thread.
2639
2640            Returns:
2641                None
2642            """
2643            for _ in range(50):
2644                other_loop_results.append(leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms))

2646
2647        other_loop_thread = threading.Thread(
2648            target=lambda: asyncio.run(other_loop_main())
2649        )
2650        other_loop_thread.start()
2651
2652        in_loop = [leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms) for _ in range(50)]
2653        in_workers = await asyncio.wait_for(
2654            asyncio.gather(
2655                *(
2656                    asyncio.to_thread(leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms, utc_ms)
2657                    for _ in range(8)
2658                )
2659            ),
2660            timeout=5,
2661        )
2662        other_loop_thread.join(timeout=5)
2663
2664        assert not other_loop_thread.is_alive()
2665        assert not gate.is_set()
2666        assert in_loop == [utc_ms + 5000] * 50
2667        assert in_workers == [utc_ms + 5000] * 8
2668        assert other_loop_results == [utc_ms + 5000] * 50
2669
2670        gate.set()
2671        self._join_refresh(leap_seconds)
2672        assert download_count() == 1
2673        assert leap_seconds._data is newer_data
2674        assert leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms) == utc_ms + 5000

2687        never map to a decreasing UTC value.

2691            leap_count (int): The leap seconds inserted up to and including it.

2698        results = [
2699            leap_seconds.tai_to_utc_ms(tai_ms)
2700            for tai_ms in range(tai_at - 2500, tai_at + 1500, 250)
2701        ]
2702
2703        assert results == sorted(results)

2705    def test_utc_to_tai_ms_matches_leapseconddata(self, data: LeapSecondData) -> None:
2706        """Test that the integer lookup table gives the same offsets as
2707        ``LeapSecondData.tai_offset`` at every threshold (+-1 ms) and on a grid of
2708        instants between 2004 and 2027.
2709
2710        Args:
2711            data (LeapSecondData): The frozen test data.
2712
2713        Returns:
2714            None
2715        """
2716        leap_seconds = LeapSeconds()
2717        epoch = LeapSeconds.ITS_EPOCH_UTC
2718        epoch_offset = data.tai_offset(epoch, check_validity=False)
2719        instants = [
2720            (leap.start - epoch) // datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1) + delta
2721            for leap in data.leap_seconds
2722            for delta in (-1, 0, 1)
2723        ]
2724        instants += list(range(0, 740_000_000_000, 7_919_999_999))
2725
2726        for utc_ms in instants:
2727            when = epoch + datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=utc_ms)
2728            expected = utc_ms + (
2729                data.tai_offset(when, check_validity=False) - epoch_offset
2730            ) // datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1)
2731            assert leap_seconds.utc_to_tai_ms(utc_ms) == expected, utc_ms

2855    def test_build(self, frozen_leap_second_data: LeapSecondData) -> None:
2856        """Test that ``build`` keeps the data and derives, for each leap second, its
2857        UTC start, the TAI start of the inserted second and the offset relative to
2858        the ITS epoch.
2859
2860        Args:
2861            frozen_leap_second_data (LeapSecondData): The frozen test data.
2862
2863        Returns:
2864            None
2865        """
2866        table = _OffsetTable.build(frozen_leap_second_data)
2867
2868        count = len(frozen_leap_second_data.leap_seconds)
2869        assert table.data is frozen_leap_second_data
2870        assert table.base_offset_ms == -32_000
2871        assert len(table.utc_starts_ms) == len(table.offsets_ms) == count
2872        assert len(table.leap_tai_starts_ms) == count
2873        post_epoch = [
2874            (utc, offset)
2875            for utc, offset in zip(table.utc_starts_ms, table.offsets_ms, strict=True)
2876            if utc >= 0
2877        ]
2878        assert post_epoch == [
2879            (_utc_its_ms(iso), leap_count * 1000)
2880            for iso, leap_count in LEAP_SECOND_INSTANTS
2881        ]
2882        for utc, tai, offset in zip(
2883            table.utc_starts_ms, table.leap_tai_starts_ms, table.offsets_ms, strict=True
2884        ):
2885            assert tai == utc + offset - 1000

2972@pytest.mark.parametrize(
2973    argnames=("candidate_until", "current_until", "expected"),
2974    argvalues=[
2975        (2, 1, True),
2976        (1, 2, False),
2977        (1, 1, False),
2978        (None, 1, False),
2979        (1, None, True),
2980        (None, None, False),
2981    ],
2982    ids=["later", "earlier", "same", "candidate_none", "current_none", "both_none"],
2983)
2984def test__is_newer(
2985    frozen_leap_second_data: LeapSecondData,
2986    candidate_until: int | None,
2987    current_until: int | None,
2988    expected: bool,
2989) -> None:
2990    """Test ``_is_newer``, where missing validity counts as the oldest.
2991
2992    Args:
2993        frozen_leap_second_data (LeapSecondData): The frozen test data.
2994        candidate_until (int | None): Year of the candidate's ``valid_until``.
2995        current_until (int | None): Year of the current ``valid_until``.
2996        expected (bool): The expected result.
2997
2998    Returns:
2999        None
3000    """
3001
3002    def with_year(year: int | None) -> LeapSecondData:
3003        """Build the test data with ``valid_until`` in ``2030 + year`` (or None).
3004
3005        Args:
3006            year (int | None): Years after 2030, or None for no validity.
3007
3008        Returns:
3009            LeapSecondData: The test data with the requested validity.
3010        """
3011        until = (
3012            None
3013            if year is None
3014            else datetime.datetime(2030 + year, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
3015        )
3016        return dataclasses.replace(frozen_leap_second_data, valid_until=until)
3017
3018    assert _is_newer(with_year(candidate_until), with_year(current_until)) is expected
